utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Mr. Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your first and last name?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: My name is Tanacko Tanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please spell your first and last name for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: T-a-n-a-c-k-o T-a-n-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, could you please tell us when and where you were born.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 10th of April, 1955, in the settlement of Tabanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where is Tabanci.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Tabanci is about 12 kilometres on the Zvornik/Bijeljina road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In which municipality is this?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: The municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, before we move to specific topics, I just wanted to ask you some general things for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. Have you already provided a statement to the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, in 2002, in June it was, as a suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they warn you of your suspect status?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I received a summons, but I don't know exactly how it all goes. In the summons it said that I was called for an interview as a suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever officially informed that you were no longer a suspect?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Regardless of being informed that you have the status of a suspect, you agreed to come here and to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You are aware of the fact that you have the status of a suspect?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you asked me to ask the Court to have some parts of your testimony as -- through private session?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the situation in the republic where I live is still not so open so that you are able to publicly speak the truth. There has been a change in the relationships after the war. Some participants in the war have become the richest people there. They have a monopoly, so certain consequences arise out of speaking openly and there would be nobody special who could protect me in such a case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tanic. I will ask the Trial Chamber to allow certain parts of your testimony to be given in private session. Could you please tell us about your education and something about your career.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I completed my elementary school in Kozluk. This is 2 kilometres away from Tabanci. I completed the economic high school in Zvornik. And in 1978 I graduated from the faculty of economy in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If the witness still has the status of suspect, he's entitled to have a lawyer present in these proceedings. Would you please ask this witness whether he will waive his right to have a lawyer present while giving testimony in this case, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, this is something that we discussed yesterday. Are you prepared to testify today without the presence of your lawyer?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps this is a good opportunity to tell you that if you think that any of the questions is of such a nature that can bring you into a touchy or delicate situation, you have the right not to answer such a question. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. If we are going this far, I think it's also important that this witness should know that anything he say can and will be used against him in a courtroom as well. This is not something I've always brought up for all suspects, but since it's been started I think it's probably a good idea to give him that right. And there's also of course the right that he has to -- if he chooses to remain silent, the Court has the right to order him to speak. And in that event, material would not normally be able to be used against him, certainly not in this court and perhaps not in other international courts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's the other side of the coin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we go on, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, did you hear what the -- Mr. Prosecutor said just now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's not a problem because I said that I would speak the truth. And in principle, I have nothing to be afraid of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Just warning, nothing else, is to let you know the situation, the overall situation. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tane, could you please speak a little more slowly when you're answering the questions because everything has to be translated, everything that you're saying. Is that all right? Once you completed the faculty of economics, where did you go on from there?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I began to work in Karakaj, one of the enterprises, it was called Univerzal, and then I moved to another firm. When the war broke out I was working in the TG Birac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do as part of your work?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: In the TG Birac I was a person who analysed and planned production.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Up until the war broke out, did you serve your regular military service?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes. I served my regular military duty in 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any ranks? What did you do? And where were you in the army?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I served my military term in Zrenjanin. I was there for six months in the medical corps. I was a regular soldier. And then I was transferred to Bihac where I served for another five months.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is Bihac in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get married?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: After I served my regular military term, I got married.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where is your wife from?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: My wife is from Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And which ethnicity is she?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Her father is a Muslim and her mother is a Serb from Lika.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, when the war broke out did you join the army? Were you militarily active?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: When the war started up until late April, I wasn't engaged in any units. When Zvornik fell, I was not in the army. In the latter part of April, I received my mobilisation summons and then I reported to the barracks. This was in the second half of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, did the Army of Republika Srpska exist at that time or was this the TO that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, this was still the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any specific tasks in the army?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't get any specific tasks. When I arrived there, we spent several days in the barracks without any duties. And then afterwards when we were organised as the Zvornik detachment during the military review, one of the superior officers -- I told one of the superior officers that I couldn't do that. The way they phrased it: God help us heroes, and are we going to go to Divic and so on. I told them I couldn't do that. I told my colleagues who were in the line-up together with me. And they said, well, you should tell them. They told me that I should inform somebody about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To tell them what?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: That I couldn't go and take part in this war the way it was being done. The way it began was very ugly. There was a lot of looting and robberies. This is something that was not for me. I was not suited to anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So did you tell somebody about that?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I told this man called Ljubomir Tesanovic that I couldn't do that. And he simply told me: Well, that's not a problem. There's work for you as well. That day, from that unit, it was only myself and another man who said that we did not wish to participate in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what period this was.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: This was sometime before the action on Kula, so it was sometime around the 21st or the 22nd of April. I'm not sure exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said at one point that the officer at the time, Tesanovic, said that there is other work for you?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us if you received any specific assignments after that, after you did not agree to join the armed combat.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Shortly before this action against Kula, whatever it's called, I was informed that I can stay in the barracks if I took a broom and started to sweep. So I took the broom and began sweeping. I agreed to do that. I did this work up until late October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that, in your opinion, some kind of retaliation or response because you refused to take up arms and go to the front?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, at the time it suited me. I would not be participating in actions; I would stay there. It didn't matter that I had to sweep the floor. There were other tasks perhaps. The brigade was in the process of being formed, but I didn't really expect them to help me very much there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From October 1992, what tasks did they assign to you?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: From October 1992 - I think it was October at least - I moved to the finances of the brigade and worked there as a cashier. And I was also chief of finances there for a time up until June or July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly what your job entailed.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, quite simply, I worked with information gathering from the terrain through personnel about the situation in the battalions; that's how it was organised. And then on the basis of the money coming in and the lists we had, through the clerks, I would hand out the money. And they would give me a receipt for what I had issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who secured the financial resources for the army?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't be quite specific, but from the very beginning it went through the municipality. The municipality provided the financial resources every month. Later on - I don't know exactly when - but it went by the corps through the state, the army -- actually the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were the officers paid in the same way, paid their salaries in the same way?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Active duty officers or rather officers of the Jugoslav army did not receive salaries from the funds that were allotted to us from the municipality and from the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In that year 1993, who was the command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: In 1993 the commander of the brigade was Vinko Pandurevic, from the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the command of the Zvornik Brigade, did you stay there throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout the whole war with an interruption in July when I went to carry out some other assignments for 30 or 40 days in the TG of Birac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who you were subordinated to, who did you work for, who did you belong to formation and establishment-wise.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the finances, the finances were under the direct control of the brigade commander, or rather, the assistant commander for the rear, for logistics, when he wasn't there. Then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you belong to the logistics department or the logistics service?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know. I wasn't interested in the establishment of it and what formation I belonged to, but I was responsible to the brigade commander for the situation in the financial department and the cash flow. And then I had chief of finance in the next part of 1993 when I remained the cashier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we are still in 1993? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're drawing to a close, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From that year 1992 until 1995, were you in any armed struggle at all, any armed combat?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I was never in any armed combat at all. I did go once and I said that in my first statement I took money up to the front line on one occasion. That was above Srebrenica. It might have been precisely in 1993 when they parachuted packages into the area. And perhaps another occasion, but I was carrying money. I didn't take part in any fighting. I went up to the front line to take the money there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, during the war years from 1992 to 1995, did you ever meet Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us please when you met him and how you met him?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, I met Dragan Jokic through his sister because she worked together with me in Standard, the Standard company, as a cashier.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And was his sister there throughout the war as well?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: She stayed there -- but actually she wasn't there until the end of the war because she went on maternity leave to give birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why she didn't come back to the army after the maternity leave? Did she come into conflict with Obrenovic at all? Did she quarrel with him?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was your impression of Dragan Jokic? What kind of man was he?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, in addition to me working with his sister, we got to know each other and had connections because he was an active officer in Bihac and his wife was from Bihac. So we would joke now and again, and meet now and again. And talking to his sister and talking to him I condemned the war, of course. And I tried to evade them as much as I could. Of course, we did exchange opinions about the situation. We agreed on some points but not on all of them of course. You can't avoid some issues; if you're there, you can't run away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In talking to him did you ever hear him express nationalistic feelings and hatred toward another nation or ethnic group? Did he condemn the Muslim nation at all?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. He knew through his sister that my wife was a Muslim, but that was never raised. And between 1992 and 1993, that was a fairly unfortunate set of circumstances. I sort of buried my head in the sand and pretended nobody knew about it, but most people did know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was Dragan Jokic an ambitious career officer?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, not at all. At the beginning of the war and at the end of the war he remained with the same rank. He had the same rank. The others who came later were promoted far faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, in that year of 1995, the month of June, were you in the command of the Zvornik Brigade then, too?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you were, where was your office located?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: As far as my office and the premises are concerned -- are you asking about 1995?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, in 1995 my offices were on the ground floor opposite the legal department offices of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, who was the commander and chief of staff at the time in the Zvornik Brigade, and I'm talking about July 1995.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: The commander, as far as I know, was Vinko Pandurevic. And the chief of staff was Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it an organised command? Did you have any morning duties in the military sense?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: It was exceptionally well-organised. The barracks were organised as a proper military barracks. And every morning we raised the flag and had a review of the rear units. And in the evening, the flag would be lowered. We had the same ceremony. And after the review of troops before breakfast, there would be a session of reporting to the commander at 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell us who conducted the review of troops and lined the troops up. Who conducted this part of the affairs, military affairs?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: As far as the review of troops was concerned it was due to the brigade commander who did this and in his absence it was the chief of staff. And the troops were lined up by the duty officer in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the usual customary daily procedure?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Every single day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to move on and focus your attention to some questions that have to do with specific dates. Do you remember those days when Srebrenica fell, that is to say the middle of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember where you yourself were and what tasks and assignments you were performing?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: From July -- actually from July onwards I was working as the cashier in the financial department of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How did you come to learn of the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, quite simply -- actually, before Srebrenica fell there were units there, they were gathering. I saw some before Srebrenica. And then afterwards, a day or two later, information arrived -- or it didn't arrive. We heard that Srebrenica had been taken over, taken control of and fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you by the by, were you in charge of any weapons or issued any weapons? Did you have any weapons actually?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, behind my cashier's desk I did have a rifle, an M-48.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And where were you on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: On the 14th of July, I was in Standard, the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember whether there were the usual activities of lining up the troops, raising the flag, and so on, on that particular morning?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I really can't say about that morning, probably there was because we never missed a day so I assume that happened that day, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you spend the morning hours of that day, the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: In the Standard compound, in my offices, in the compound itself, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you happen to notice any unusual activity on that morning of the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Nothing special, except that there was this general commotion over Srebrenica. And I don't know. There were -- there was different information coming in about the fighting above Srebrenica and the forests there and the problems, so that kind of thing, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we go into private session now for a moment, please, Your Honour, just briefly for a portion of the testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanackovic -- Tanic, excuse me, do you recall whether at any time you had contacts with the duty operation officers in the Zvornik Brigade command for the purposes of your job?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, never, except if they had a message from the commander to pass on to me telling me to do something. But they themselves did not have the capacity to issue orders to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Why do you say that the duty operations officer could not issue orders to you?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, simply because the duty operations officer had the task of collecting and passing on information. And at the briefings at 7.00 a.m., he would report on the situation in the battalions, who was requesting what and so on and so forth. And then on the basis of that and of our reports, the commander would issue tasks to all those present.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Dragan Jokic as the duty operations officer ever issue a personal order to you, or rather, had he done that would you have been duty-bound to respect it, to comply with it?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there also a barracks duty officer at the time?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes. The barracks duty officer lined up the troops, organised the review and the raising and lowering of the flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether on that day new conscripts were being seen off to the army in the barracks compound in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: It's possible, but I can't recall whether that happened precisely on that day. But it is possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I wanted to ask you what happened next. Did you go and take up the task of guarding those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I took my rifle. I got into a little van. There were five or six of us. The shift, they knew me and I probably knew them at that time. But so much time has passed that I can't now recall all the names of the people who were there. They all knew me because it was I who gave out the money and they would come to see me for their pay slips and such like. But right now I can't recall who the men were that I went with in that little van.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you told what the fate of those prisoners was to be?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell me whether any of the officers or senior officers of the Zvornik Brigade was in that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing any of the officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you sitting in front or in the back with the men?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: In the back with the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: We arrived at the school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did those soldiers get out of the vehicle with you?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what unit these men belonged to if you don't know them personally?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I think it was the shift from Jelacici. I don't know if it can be established now what group that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us where this place Jelacici is?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I was never up there because it was towards the line in the direction of Sekovici. But I don't know precisely because I was never there. I just remembered the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Orahovac, did you see any officers or commanders there?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: : (Private Session)

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in front of the school, did you observe that they had started taking prisoners away?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes. I forgot to mention that there were already two dead on the playground covered up, probably in their own clothes. This was on the playground. And I saw a heap of clothes in front of the entrance to the gym. I think there was a crutch there as well. And they had already started boarding the truck. That was when I went to sit on the school steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you present when the two prisoners of war were executed?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. They were already dead when I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any protests? Was there any anger? Were there any demands made by the prisoners that they should not leave the gym?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know what happened. I know that at one point there was talk of all of them going to be exchanged. They were persuaded to get on to the truck, and then they were taken off to the execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At any point did you see any building construction machinery nearby?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me what was used to take the prisoners away from the gym, what kind of vehicle.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I saw a small truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a military or a civilian truck?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say. The tarpaulin on military trucks was not always the proper colour for military trucks, so I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point you said you went up to the school?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason? Why did you go away from the place where the prisoners were being boarded on to a truck?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't want to hang around there. I didn't want to be close to that. I simply moved off as far as I was able, to get out of the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any authority that would have allowed you to prevent anything like that?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Certainly not. In the war, I did only what I had to. I had no authority. I tried to get through the war in the best way possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point see executions and killings of prisoners of war being carried out in front of the gym?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How far is the house to which you went from the gym?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: It's in the back behind the gym, not very far from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said at one point what the name was of the man into whose house you went. Do you remember it now?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: After that I went to Mira Vidovic, the municipality cashier. I knew her and so I dropped in and stayed there until about 11.00 p.m. I told the men to pick me up on their way back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From the house where you were, could you hear gunfire?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. The second house was further away. First I went to a forester's house, and when I had had some brandy I went to see Mira. And I sat there until the evening, until 11.00 p.m. approximately. I didn't have a watch, but it was already getting dark. So it was certainly past 9.00 and more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From that place could you hear any gunfire?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Not while I was inside the house, but when I got out of the house intending to perhaps walk to the barracks, I had hardly passed 100 metres when I heard firing from the up above where Streliste was and the side. And then I stopped. I thought someone might hit me. I might be hit by a stray bullet. So I waited there for someone I knew to come by and give me a lift.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was this synchronised or random shooting?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say now, but certainly you could hear shooting, both above Orahovac and from the side. Yes, you could hear gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we just go into private session for a minute because of the questions that I am about to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, at one point you said that the people condemned what was going on?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What is this conclusion of yours based on?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: It's based on the fact that, for example, I lived in a village and 90 per cent of the people there were saying: What is going on? Why is this being done? Perhaps there were about 10 people who would say things like: They should all be killed, and so on. But I believe it was a small number of people who were prepared to do that, and this was obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You personally at that point, in that place, did you condemn such actions?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes. In conversations and also just when I was thinking to myself. At one point I thought: Well, it's not a problem if I took a rifle and killed a Serb or two. But then what would happen? Then they would beat me up and push me around a little bit and what would happen? Nothing. Now ten years later when I think back about it, if I had done something like that it wouldn't have meant anything much at the time, it wouldn't have made a difference, but I was outraged at the events that were going on, especially because there were children involved and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, I have been told that not everything that you said is in the transcript. Were you afraid that you would also get killed?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Had I, for example, taken it upon myself to say: What are you doing and tried to kill somebody, of course my own people would have tried to kill me back. I was outraged because of these events. But as an individual, I couldn't do much. People of authority in that place and other places where this was going on could have done something because the mood of the -- the public mood was against these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point you said that there were also young men there, young people.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I saw two young boys who were carrying water. When my van stopped in the evening, there was a boy of 7 or 8 years old who had survived the executions. When we entered the Standard compound he was saying he was from Srebrenica, asking where his father was. We went out and they took the boy to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you: What time of day was it when you walked from Orahovac towards the barracks?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Let's say it was about 10.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How far is the barracks from Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know, about 8 kilometres approximately. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The fact that you went on foot, is that the result of your intention to leave that place at any price?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: It was already late. I left those killing fields and I was just looking for a way to go home -- actually to go to Standard. There was no way to go home. I went to the road and then I thought, well, I'll just start walking and perhaps, who knows, somebody will pass by.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us which vehicle was it? Who was operating that vehicle? Did you know that soldier?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: The driver was Gotovac, Djordje Gotovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was he coming back from Orahovac or from positions?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: From Orahovac. He was at the killing site in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How many soldiers were there in that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, that's a bit difficult to say. I cannot remember. I know I was there; that young man; Mihajlo Stevanovic was there; then probably Sreten was there; Miladin Mijatovic. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't understand the last sentence the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you left the house and started walking towards the barracks, could you still hear the firing?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have some problems with the transcript. The interpreter says that she did not understand the last sentence the witness said. The question is: "How many soldiers were there in that vehicle?" Witness, would you please repeat your answer again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know I was there, the young man who survived; Mihajlo Stevanovic was there, and well, the driver. I cannot tell you for sure. I'm not sure whether Miladin Mijatovic and Sreten Milosevic were also in the van. I'm not sure. I don't know actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when you came -- when you arrived at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I think I got there at 11.30, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was this on the 14th of July? Once you came to the barracks, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Is this private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not this part.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: We need to move into private session and then I will tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we can respect the wishes of the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tanic, we have information here that on that day, the 14th and the 15th, Dragan Jokic was the duty operations officer in the Zvornik Brigade. Did you ever on that evening have any kind of contact with Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Dragan Jokic anywhere that evening?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No -- I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where is the duty operations officer's room?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: That office is on the first floor to the right, the first to the right. Then there's Sreten Milosevic's office and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And where is your room? Is that on the first floor? On the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I've already said that it was on the ground floor across from the legal affairs office and the military police office.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you spend the entire night in your office?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point did you see a bus with prisoners in the barracks compound?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us where the bus was.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: As far as I could see, it was in front of the reception area, inside the compound in front of the reception area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there people securing the bus, guarding the bus?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything in particular, because the military police was manning the gate. So it wasn't any special security. I didn't notice anything special.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice if there were any people in the bus, whether the bus was full?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you address any of the people at the reception area, any of the military police personnel?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ask any questions about the bus with the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I'm going to move now to the second part of my questions relating to the 15th of July, perhaps, Your Honours, it would be a good point to go on a break. I have been informed that this last answer was not recorded in the transcript. So if you agree I would just like to repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Tanic, if you talked to anybody about the prisoners. Did you show any interest in these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll take a break here, and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, please continue your direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you remember we took a break and left off discussing the 14th of July into the 15th when you arrived in the command of the Zvornik Brigade. You remember that, do you?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that you spent the night at the command of the Zvornik Brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when you got up. Do you remember whether there were any activities on the morning of the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the specifics. There was general commotion, if I can put it that way, that day. I can't really remember whether there was a review of troops or not, but all I can say is that one day there was a troop review and that it was conducted by Pandurevic and that of the members of the military police there were just four or five of them lined up. Because Drago let the others go because there were the deaths and Pandurevic then ordered that everybody should come back. Now, what day that was that happened, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us why he ordered all the military policemen to return.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, he was sort of angry and he said: Why did you send them home? They're like chickens -- got killed like chickens, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On that morning of the 15th of July, did you see Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the duty of informing the duty officer or Dragan Jokic of everything?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, I had no obligations vis-a-vis the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it your duty to tell the duty officer what you had done the previous day, that is to say the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, I just had the obligation, or rather, my chief was obliged to go and report and submit a report as to what assignments we had carried out on any particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps this is a good opportunity for me to ask you: Who did your chief refer to, report to?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: As 0700 hours, he reported to the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And if the brigade commander was absent, who would your chief report to about what your service had done?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: The chief of staff then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And who on the morning of the 15th of July was the chief of staff?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I think it was Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please, whether you know that during those days in the Zvornik area there were other mass killings as well?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How did you come to learn about that and how was the story told and the message conveyed?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, in principle people know everything. You can digress in the Zvornik Brigade and others, but the characteristic thing was that when an operation was being planned, it was the women in the village who knew about this first before even the soldiers. So people knew everything that went on and where it went on. So in my first statement I said that there were 7 or 8.000 killed according to what I knew in the different locations, Kozluk, Branjevo, Djeverici [phoen] or wherever.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any information -- official information given to the soldiers that these mass crimes had taken place, or was it just that people commented?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. People just commented. There was never anything official, any official publication or anything like that. And they tried to hush things up and stop or lessen the tension and stories and rumours that were going around.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And on what basis did you conclude that they tried to hush things up, cover things up?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, if I can put it this way, people realised that everybody knew about it. And then afterwards, some grave sites were found and some were unearthed. And they realised that it was a mistake and that now they had to, if I can put it this way, annul it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So in the talks and tales going around by the army and the soldiers and the locals, did they condemn the operation or support it?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: For the most part, as I've already said, 90 per cent of the people, or rather, a very large number of the inhabitants condemned it and so did the soldiers, condemned what had happened. But this mass of people was not enough to do anything. It wasn't a critical mass large enough to turn things around. And until those people are tried over there, there will be problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You yourself, Mr. Tanic, did you have the obligation of informing everybody -- anybody about what you did on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. Because the chief went to report, and he's the only person that I can talk to. But it was common knowledge that I was there. I don't wish to deny it. I was in Orahovac on the 14th, and I'm not challenging that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, this position, as you described it a moment ago, was it the reason you decided to come into court here and testify publicly about all those events?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, except for the portions of my testimony which were given in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We would like to assure you that you have no need to fear; it was in private session. Now, in addition to the fact that you are conscious of being a suspect and the fact that you decided to come here and tell the truth immediately after talking to me, is that right, you have nothing to hide?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, I have nothing to hide with respect to Srebrenica and all the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any time throughout these events that came to follow after those tragic days hear anything at all about the participation of Dragan Jokic in those activities?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. I never heard anything, except for the fact that he went about his business.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody comment and say that Dragan Jokic was in a position to prevent this or stop it?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. Nobody said anything along those lines. They wouldn't have taken it seriously. They tried to lessen the importance of people not close to them. That's my conclusion at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself suffer any unpleasantness due to the fact that you already had an interview with the Prosecution and that you were on the spot in Orahovac on that 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, I did not, except I feel the burden of it myself, having been there on that date. Yes, people asked me: Did I say anything, was it recorded, and so on, but I didn't give any comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you something about the bus with the prisoners on the 15th before noon. You mentioned the bus. So when you got up on the morning of the 15th, do you remember having seen that bus in the compound of the barracks?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember when the bus left?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I know that there was some buses, that they were passing by and that the buses were going. They would say: They're going off to Pilica. That's what the stories going around were, but I didn't see it. But I do know that there were buses coming and going and in Pilica they didn't want to receive them, they were returned, sent back. And then I don't know where he ended up, perhaps in Petkovci or wherever.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tanic, did you ever hear any comments among the soldiers to the effect that Dragan Jokic was the scapegoat in all this prior to his leaving for The Hague?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, in principle people were rather surprised to hear that he is being held responsible in view of the engineer's work he was doing. He wasn't a person who issued orders, so people were surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tanic, for being as frank and forthright with your answers. You will now perhaps be asked something by Mr. Karnavas and Ms. Issa from the Prosecution and Their Honours. So I should like to ask you to answer those questions, if there are any, but thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Karnavas, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just may ask a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas:.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said you were outraged on what you had seen on that particular day on the 14th. Obviously you knew that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, well, we didn't have the answer in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So obviously you knew that they were being executed?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, at that point in time when it had already started in Orahovac when I got there and when you could see that they had this intention and that they were sending some for the exchange not to -- they weren't treated as prisoners of war but were executed, that's when I realised. But I couldn't assume anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But at some point while you were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, not sending them for an exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But at some point while you were there you realised that they were going to or were in fact being executed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And that's -- you drew yourself away from those activities, as you've indicated?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You went to somebody's house and --

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Right behind the school. I didn't leave straight away. I sat behind the school. I saw young boys carrying water and we commented. And then I went to the next building, the gym hall, the sports hall. So I couldn't see what was going on. Then I went to a house that was further away, much further away from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, before doing that did you ever walk up to Drago Nikolic to try to dissuade him from carrying out these activities?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. It never entered my head, never occurred to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, what would I be doing that for? I wasn't in a position to do so. I'm an ordinary soldier and he would have eliminated me straight away. And he'd say I was mad. So how could I go up to him and say: Don't you do that? I didn't have the authority to do that in view of the job I did. I just wasn't in a position to go up to somebody like that and tell him. I could talk to him privately and say: You shouldn't do that. But in that mass of people and once they had already taken the decision themselves - not asking anybody, I don't know who they asked - I wasn't in a position to influence Drago to do anything about it. I just wasn't in a position to do that. It would have been madness on my part. He would have eliminated me either physically or in some other way. Anyway, he would have got rid of me one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Why do you say that. Why would Drago, as you put it, first-name basis, why would he do something like that to you? After all, who is he or who was he at the time who could do that?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: He was, how do you say that, the security officer in the brigade. Now, what all that entails -- he was in charge of security matters. We called him the security officer in the brigade. But establishment-wise, I don't know his exact position. But as far as I was concerned he looked a bit angry. Maybe he's a good man, I don't know. But I tried to keep out of his way. Just say hello in passing and that would be it. Good day, and that's it. The less contact with him, the better.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know who Popovic was at the time or at least what position he held within the VRS?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I did not know nor did I see him. I didn't know how come an officer was there and who the officer was. And I asked somebody from the military police: Who is that man. And they told me he was Popovic from the corps. And from the corps I just know the man working in the finances, Pajic Damir was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when you returned later on that evening you said that you met certain individuals, officers who had been there during the day, ordering and carrying out these executions, correct, when you returned to Standard?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Is this a private session now? Are we in closed session? Do you want me to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We're not mentioning any names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe at first we should not mention any names. Later on if you need, you have to mention some names, we could easily go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not interested in the names of the individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking: When you came back later on that night you met with those same individuals who had been out there carrying out those executions or ordering those executions?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And that's when they said they were going to have a special dinner?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, you've done a good job, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were congratulating themselves, a job well-done, executing innocent people?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I take it you were repulsed or outraged by their behaviour as well when they were carrying on in that fashion.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I refused. I didn't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. And then as I believe you indicated, from there you went to your office where you had a bunk and you went to sleep. You stayed away from them?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I take it you didn't tell anybody regarding these -- what you had seen at Orahovac out of fear?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. I said that at home. I told my friends, anyone I knew, everyone I knew. How else could I have gone through this without talking about it? I didn't conceal it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. But I'm saying on that specific night. You've already indicated that you never stopped at the duty officer's -- at the operation room to at least inform the duty officer what you had seen and who had carried out what. Right?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you also did not go to Obrenovic's office to tell Obrenovic what you had seen. Right?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And he was the acting commander at the time, was he not, since Pandurevic was gone?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Probably, I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I think Pandurevic was in charge of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. The killing operation?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Srebrenica. The taking of Srebrenica. The military operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. But you knew Obrenovic, did you not, by person?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I didn't. From 1992 to 1995, I knew all of the officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: From the lowest ranking to the highest ranking. From the first chief of the TO onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Right. I just want to make sure that you knew him. When you saw him, you knew, this is Obrenovic. Right?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you knew his position?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Chief of staff, number two, Pandurevic being number one. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then there was Sreten Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Now, on that particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's no need to hurry --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise if I seem a little bit anxious to you. I'm not. Maybe it's that extra coffee I had during the break. But needless to say I just want to pinpoint a couple of issues. When you came back you never went to Obrenovic's office, chief of staff, to say: Mr. Obrenovic, major, whatever he was at the time, there's killings going on in Orahovac. You didn't do that on the evening of the 14th when you came back?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, no. No one did, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But we're speaking about you. I'm not talking about --

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm speaking about that particular night. You never went there to see him?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't talk to him the next morning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that coffee is really effective. Slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I apologise, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't speak to him the next day on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And when Pandurevic came back from the field - and he's a pretty impressive kind of guy, right, when he walks in you see him, you know who he is, he has this aura of leadership, right? - you didn't walk up to him and say, commander, there's been some executions going on?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My last question. I know you were outraged and I believe you. But could you please explain to us why, why didn't you tell Obrenovic on the 14th, who clearly was there or the duty officer or Pandurevic when he came back the 15th, why didn't you ever go to their offices and say: This was what happened; something needs to be done?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: That would have been meaningless on my part. First of all, because they knew what had happened and it wasn't necessary for me to inform them. I don't know what my role would have been if I had gone and said, Mr. Obrenovic, such-and-such things had been done when it was general knowledge. It wouldn't be news to him. And secondly, there would have been sanctions against me. I might have been punished. I might have been sent to the front line. This would have been confrontational.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it might have been well-known to Mr. Obrenovic, but you have no reason to believe that this was known to Mr. Jokic, do you?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I can say in general that on the territory of the municipality everybody knew. There had been executions. Everybody -- it was common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the 14th --

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: On the 14th. The news gets around right away. Everybody knew that executions were going on in Orahovac. Some people escaped and there were problems with the pit. And everybody knew everything. It went around -- well, not exactly the same minute, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So I take it that before you went to Orahovac, you knew that executions were going on?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I know only that there were executions in the woods and everywhere. There were all kinds of stories going around. It was chaos. I can't tell you what happened on what date. On the 14th none of us who went to Orahovac knew what was going to happen until we arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I want to take it step by step because now you're saying everybody knew while it was happening. So I'm asking you concretely -- I'm asking you concretely --

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before you went to Orahovac did you know executions were about to happen there or were ongoing, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know. In Orahovac, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. And it was once you got there and you saw who was involved, that's when you realised what was happening?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And when you came back from Orahovac, you never told anyone at the Standard what you had seen, did you?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I told my colleagues, the journalists, my friends, the people who were around, not the same evening but on the 15th in the morning. We commented on these events, not on the 15th at midnight, no. After midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about on the 14th because you're making the assumption --

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: On the 14th, no, because the 15th was a new day. On the 14th, I didn't talk to anyone because it was nearly midnight and then it was the next day after -- and then I went to my office. And I didn't talk to anyone about what had happened until the morning. But on the following day everybody commented on what had happened. And in those six or seven days, there were many events that occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: So I can't really pinpoint it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So who ordered whose executions, since everybody was talking about that? Was it Obrenovic? Pandurevic? Popovic? Beara? Who were the ones who ordered the executions?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't have this information. I don't know who did it. I don't know who ordered it. They probably know, but I don't. I don't know who ordered this to be done, what they did. I don't know. I can hypothesise. It would take quite some time. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't want you to hypothesise. Well, thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Any cross-examination, Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, I do have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I just want to pick up from you just indicating in the last exchange that essentially everybody knew what was going on, everybody knew about the executions during that period. That's what you said. Right?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: They knew when it had already been done, but none of us -- most of us didn't know that there would be executions. But at the beginning of the executions and while this was going on, after that it was common knowledge. But at that moment it wasn't common knowledge that they were to be shot. Most people didn't know it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to turn to your interview in Banja Luka when you were speaking to the OTP. You stand by what you told the OTP during that period of time. Right? You stand by what you said to the investigators when they met with you in Banja Luka. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I think I said that. I may have added a few names, but all the names I mentioned I repeated the same names. I abide by that. I may have made an error, perhaps, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But I'm not asking you about names right now. I'm just asking you generally, in general, when you met with the investigators --

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I abide by this. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So I just want to go over some of the things that you may have -- you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can ask the assistance of Mr. Usher. And I would be referring to page 77 in the English transcript and page 64 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I'm just starting about in the middle about line -- a little bit above line 14 in your version, sir. And you were asked a question: "The next day did you learn people were being executed at other sites?" And you answer: "It might be, so I cannot be specific about it, but usually something would happen. On that day it would become knowledge or it would become known on the same day." And then you were asked another question: "Would I be right in saying that the day after you were at Orahovac most people knew what had happened including Zvornik civilians?" And you say: "Yes, and politicians knew and soldiers knew and civilians knew." You stand by that statement. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, earlier you were also asked about building machines in the examination-in-chief, whether you saw building machines when you were --

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recall being asked that?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like you then to -- in the English version we're turning to page 59 in the interview, in the transcript. And if you can then please turn to page 50 in your version, please. Just if we can perhaps start around the middle. You were asked: "When did you find out about the graves being dug for those people that were executed on the day that you were there?" And you say: "I think people that were captured, they saw the machines, they saw the machines passing by and they probably got very upset. I don't know." And then you're asked: "Did you see machines passing by on the day that you were at the gymnasium?" And you say: "No, I did not but those machines passed along the road before that." You stand by that as well, sir: "Those machines passed along the road before that"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was for this reason that during my examination-in-chief I asked the witness whether he had seen any machinery, and the answer was no --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question today is practically asking the witness to speculate. He did not see any machinery; that was his direct response. That is why I think this question is not in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think just because you asked this question and the witness answered no so that the Prosecution will show the witness his previous statement and ask some questions on that effect. There's some differences between the situation at the gymnasium or on the road and we'll look into the transcript to see that. And we also remembered the answer of this witness. He said he thinks. Well, Ms. Issa, you may proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So, sir, you stand by that answer that you gave to the interviewers in Banja Luka, that those machines had passed along the road before that, before you had gotten to the gymnasium? You have --

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I think they passed by before and that they became restless and tried to break down the door. And then those two were shot. But I wasn't in Orahovac then. I hadn't arrived then. This all happened before I arrived in Orahovac. And I think the machinery passed by, but I didn't see it and I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So how do you -- what makes you think that the machines were there before that?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Because people were saying that that's why they were upset, they had come to the door. I don't know whether they had been able to see anything, that they had tried to break out, and that's how those two that I saw lying dead in the playground were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say people were saying that the machines were there before that, who are you referring to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: They didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's not what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We could look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do I know?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, what people are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know. There are many people there, lots of people there. I can't say there were 100, because you would ask me: How do you know? Did you count? Because there were a lot of people. And in the group I was with, I didn't know them all. There was general talk going around.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So are you talking about the soldiers that were there in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think we might need to go into private session for the next few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you, sir, about the child, the 7-year-old boy you said in your chief that he was saved and he was in the van with you when you returned back to the barracks on the 14th, the night of the 14th of July. Now, can you tell us first of all what makes you think that he was saved.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: He did survive the execution. He was taken out, but he survived. I couldn't really tell you the details. But simply, there were some who survived. They were returned to Standard. We left, and he was taken to the hospital. I don't know if he was just grazed by a bullet or something.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, where was he -- where was he taken before he was taken to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: This was between 11.00 and midnight. We left Standard and the driver took him to the hospital. He wasn't taken anywhere prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how do you --

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember that anything else happened as far as I recall. I think that's how it was, but I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But how do you know specifically that he survived the executions?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
