utterances.text: Because the person who was also there told me about it, and he came with us. He was taken out because he was grazed, and he was taken to the hospital to be bandaged. He was lightly wounded, grazed. The boy was talking where Srebrenica is or asking where it was, where his father was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And where was he picked up from?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there at the time. I was in front waiting. The van came along, and I got into the van. The boy was already inside, so I don't know those details.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware, sir, of the approximately 15 wounded prisoners that were at the Standard in the barracks -- or at the clinic at the Standard in the barracks on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No. I wasn't. If I could add anything, this would be about this other group that I know about. But this was later -- but perhaps we could close it a little bit and I could say it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: That was another group.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I think perhaps -- I'm not sure if the witness is requesting that we go into private session, Your Honour, but perhaps we could do that and he could clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, what do you mean by saying that we could close --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About this other group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. What do you mean by saying that, we could close it a little bit and I could say it again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What sense? I don't know. When was this? What --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there's some -- maybe some language differences.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm wondering if Your Honour would allow me to ask a question just to try to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed, but just be cautious that we would return back to private session at any time. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you were saying there was this other group that you could tell us about. Right?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Like this or in a closed session? How do you do it? Should we do it like this or in a closed session. About this other group, about these 15 people that you're asking about, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Are you asking that we go into private session, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session. You may proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, earlier you were telling us how people were outraged and had condemned the executions and what occurred. So it would be fair to say that the public was quite upset about what had been going on, all the executions that were going on in this period. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that during that time, either on the 14th or the 15th of July, there was something aired on television showing Serb bodies? You weren't aware of that?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, no. I only know that a certain number of soldiers were killed. I think the number of casualties was about 40. I think that included eight military police officers and then a certain number from each battalion. There were also some men who were wounded. The casualties numbered about 40 men. I don't know about the other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If you don't know, that's fine. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Issa. Any re-direct, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one thing that we need to clarify, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tanic, in Banja Luka and today you said the next day already there was a lot of talk about what had happened, about the executions, and that 90 per cent of the people condemned this. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the next day," that is what you said to the Prosecution on page 64 of the B/C/S version, this is what you told the investigators in Banja Luka, which day would this be chronologically? When you say "the next day," from what day?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: The 15th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness has already answered that question. Do you have any other questions?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I apologise. I think that was maybe taken out of context because I read out another portion of the -- of what the witness had said earlier. So I'm not sure -- I would suggest that perhaps the question was misstating things slightly. But he has answered the question. I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think he has answered the question. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us then finish with this: Mr. Tanic, in contacts with Dragan Jokic did you ever hear or at any other time did you hear from Dragan Jokic or anyone else about the participation of Dragan Jokic in all of this?

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This question has been asked and answered at least for three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wanted to confirm this because of the cross-examination, because the question was asked about the possible knowledge of Dragan Jokic on the 14th of July. We have no problem about the 15th of July, Your Honour. We also said that in our opening statement. This is something that is repeated by the witness today. The whole of Zvornik knew what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Argibay, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Yes, sir, you were talking today a little earlier about that it was your chief's obligation to report either to the commander or the chief of staff. And I wanted to know: Who was your chief? And I don't want the name, only the position.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: My chief from July 1993 was Drago Sakotic. And after --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Sorry. I don't want the name. I want the position.

utterances.speaker: TANACKO TANIC
utterances.text: Well, of course. That's not a problem. He was the chief for financial affairs. Afterwards, before Srebrenica, another man was in this post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge Argibay's question? I see everybody is shaking their heads. At this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We have no documents to tender through the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Not from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, thank you very much indeed for coming to The Hague to give your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And am I no longer considered as a suspect? What my status was before, has that now been lifted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have to consult with the Prosecutor. I'm sorry I could not give you a definite answer on the spot, but you could ask the Prosecution to clarify this issue for you. Yes. And when we are adjourned, the usher will show you out of the room. Are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise at this stage? If not, the hearing for today is adjourned. We'll resume next Monday morning, 9.00, in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 11.44 a.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of July, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
